{{Short description|Mughal era mathematician and historian}}

'''Lutfullah Muhandis''' was a 17th century [[Mughal Empire|Mughal]]-era [[mathematician]] and [[historian]].<ref name=s>{{Cite book |last=Khan |first=Nasir Raza |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Ye62EAAAQBAJ&dq=lutfullah+muhandis&pg=PA112 |title=Islam in India: History, Politics and Society |date=2023-06-09 |publisher=Taylor & Francis |isbn=978-1-000-89869-9 |pages=112–114 |language=en}}</ref>

== Biography ==
He was the second son of the architect [[Ustad Ahmad Lahori]] and brother of [[Ataullah Rashidi]]. His book ''Diwan-e-Muhandis'' discusses the artistic and architectural achievements of his father.<ref name="s" /> He was also a well-known mathematician, with a practical treatise on geometrical shapes in his credit.<ref name="o">{{Cite book |last=Necipoğlu |first=Gülru |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xHXEDwAAQBAJ&dq=Ustad+Ahmad+Lahori&pg=PA155 |title=The Topkapi Scroll: Geometry and Ornament in Islamic Architecture |date=1996-03-01 |publisher=Getty Publications |isbn=978-0-89236-335-3 |language=en|page=155}}</ref><ref name="f">{{Cite book |last1=Yasin |first1=Mohammad |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hz4LJu1EqJIC&dq=Ustad+Ahmad+Lahori&pg=PA89 |title=Reading in Indian History |last2=Yasin |first2=Madhvi |date=1988 |publisher=Atlantic Publishers & Distri |language=en|page=89}}</ref> He was also involved in [[architecture]] and completed projects in Mandu and Peshwar as well as several commissions for [[Dara Shikoh]].<ref>{{cite book |author=Chanchal Dadlani |chapter=Innovation, Appropriation, and Representation: Mughal Architectural Ornament in the Eighteenth Century |editor1=Gülru Necipoglu |editor2=Alina Payne |title=Histories of Ornament: From Global to Local |year=2016 |publisher=Princeton University Press |isbn=9780691167282 |page=381 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9nACCwAAQBAJ }}</ref>
